name: Girona Futbol Club, S.A.D.
notes: League: Girona were relegated at the end of 2025-26 (ARA, 4 Jun 2026) and play LaLiga Hypermotion (second tier) in 2026-27; the record keeps the given league key. Latest accounts are 2024-25, the Champions League season (accounts formulated 30 Sep 2025, approved at the Dec 2025 AGM): net turnover EUR 109.904m (EUR 71.953m in 2023-24), net profit EUR 16.495m (club: a historic EUR 16.5m). Breakdown: broadcast includes EUR 29.962m of UEFA market pool; commercial is shop EUR 2.042m plus sponsorship EUR 11.127m; advertising (EUR 1.477m), competitions (EUR 5.555m) and season tickets and members (EUR 3.746m) are separate, so matchday is not one stated figure. Wages are sporting-squad costs only (non-sporting staff EUR 10.392m more). The 2025-26 budget was EUR 75m; after relegation the CEO forecast about EUR 37m of operating income for 2026-27 including a EUR 16m parachute (ARA). Capacity: the club's page states 11,810, but the same page still says the team is in Primera, so it may be dated; Montilivi's UEFA capacity for 2024-25 Champions League matches was 9,721. Montilivi, Ltd is identified with Pere Guardiola because the accounts list it as the only other holder above 10% (15.8948%) and ARA describes him as owner of 16%. Beneficial-owner declaration in the accounts (30 Sep 2025) names Sheikh Mansour (47.85%) and Marcelo Claure (35.04%). Etihad's main-sponsor deal ran three seasons from 2024-25; whether it continues in Segunda is not confirmed. No valuation, attendance average, social-follower count or net debt found on a citable text page (the club's attendance, debt and revenue sheets are image-only PDFs).

ownership_summary: Girona Futbol Club, S.A.D. is owned by City Football Group (Midco) Limited with 47.85%, Marcelo Claure's MC Girona LLC with 35.04% and Montilivi, Ltd with 15.89% (Pere Guardiola, who chairs the board and is described as owner of 16%), per the 2024-25 accounts; CFG and Guardiola's Girona Football Group bought in together in 2017 and Claure joined in 2020. CFG's stake sat with Football Trustee Limited from July 2024 to July 2025 to satisfy UEFA multi-club rules; CFG itself is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour's Newton Investment and Development, with Silver Lake holding nearly 17%.
